about.title: Richmond Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails in a Richmond home, workplace, or on I-80 can change a life in seconds. Contra Costa County residents buy the same appliances, tools, medications, car parts, and children's products as anyone else in California, and when one of those items is built wrong, designed wrong, or sold without a proper warning, the law here is unusually direct. California applies strict liability to most product claims. You generally do not need to prove the manufacturer was careless; you need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That distinction matters for the roughly 110,000 people who call Richmond home, because it shifts the conversation from corporate intent to the product itself. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects injured Richmond residents with an independent product liability attorney who works on contingency. Keep the product, keep the packaging, keep your receipts, and let a lawyer sort out which company in the chain — maker, distributor, or retailer — should answer for it.

whyChoose.title: Why Richmond Residents Turn to LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict Liability Is on Your Side
items.desc: Under California law, most product cases do not require proof that the manufacturer was negligent. The attorneys in our network know how to frame a design, manufacturing, or warning defect so that the product's failure — not the company's state of mind — is what the case turns on.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Is Fair Game
items.desc: The maker, the distributor, and the store in Richmond that sold the item may all be responsible. An independent attorney can identify each company in the supply chain rather than stopping at the first name on the box.

items.title: Evidence Preservation From Day One
items.desc: The single most important piece of evidence in a product case is the product. The lawyer you are connected with will explain how to store the item, its packaging, and any remaining pieces so nothing is lost or altered before it can be examined.

items.question: My tire blew out on I-80 near Richmond and I crashed. Could that be a product liability case?
items.answer: It can be, if the tire, wheel, or another vehicle part failed because of a defect rather than ordinary wear or road debris. I-80 and Richmond Parkway carry some of the highest collision counts in the city, and not every crash there is simply driver error. Do not let the tow yard discard the tire or the vehicle; an attorney will want it inspected. LawProactive can connect you with a lawyer who handles vehicle defect claims at no cost to you.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer did something wrong?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability usually operates on strict liability, which means you need to show the product had a defect in its design, manufacture, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company intended harm or was careless is typically not the question. That said, each case has its own facts, and an attorney can tell you how the rule applies to yours.

items.question: I already threw away the broken product and the box. Is my claim gone?
items.answer: Not necessarily, though it does make the case harder. Photos, receipts, order confirmations, medical records describing the injury, and the same model still on store shelves can all help establish what the product was and how it failed. Stop discarding anything else connected to the incident right now. The attorney you are connected with can assess what evidence remains and whether it is enough to move forward.
